newsitem.title: USA: Crude prices flounder in static U.S. cash markets.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices flounder in static U.S. cash markets.

text.p: Domestic cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf continued to flounder Wednesday afternoon at steady prices levels, while refiners refused to play the grade markets for July barrels.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing steadied at $20.70-80 a barrel, but Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) remained at a 11-14 cents premium to July NYMEX futures.
July/August WTI spreads were at minus 7-13 cents, reflecting near-term bearishness.
Outrights were also tempered ahead of tonight's American Petroleum Institute (API) stock report, and were recovering from Tuesday's price shock when July futures shed 84 cents.
On the cash side of business, traders said only a handful of confirmed deals crossed their desks. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold two cents weaker than Tuesday at WTI/Cushing minus seven cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded hands in the morning at a steady $1.53 discount to the benchmark, while WTI Postings stayed close to $2.00, selling at $1.97, traders said.
"It seems a little too early for July barrels, so refiners are staying away from the market this week," said a trader.
Sweet grades were looking for direction from overseas markets, but could not find a lead. There were two unconfirmed Brent deals, but players would not reveal if trades occurred.

A Brent cargo laoding June 12-14, which was passed through paper chains and kept by BP, was reoffered late in London at July Brent -20 cents, a wide 23 cents off a trade on Tuesday and 37 cents off last week's plateau.

July Brent-WTI spreads remained around the $1.50 level. Traders said a slight narrowing had aided sweet Gulf barrels, but the trend did not overshadow the fact plentiful supplies of Brent and Nigerian barrels could be found in the Gulf.
